questions.question: Mameluke style of architecture belongs to which dynasty ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Slave dynasty.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mameluke Architecture:-**

 
 
• **Mameluke architecture **is characterized by its** use of stone, brick, and wood, as well as its rich ornamentation.**
 
• **The Mameluke style **of architecture belongs to the** Slave Sultanate.**
 
• **Common features of Mamluk architecture include:**
 
 
• **Pointed arches:** These arches are often decorated with intricate geometric patterns.
 
• **Muqarnas**: These are honeycomb-like decorative forms that are often used to create transitions between different architectural elements.
 
• **Ablaq:** This is a technique of alternating between different colors of stone, such as white and red, to create a striped effect.
 
• 
 **Mashrabiyas:** These are wooden latticework windows that are often used to filter light and provide privacy.
 
 
 
 
 
 
• 
 **Slave dynasty:-**

 
 
• 
 The Slave dynasty, also known as the Mamluk dynasty, was a dynasty of Indian sultans of Turkish origin that ruled over Delhi Sultanate from 1206 to 1290 CE.
 
 
• 
 The dynasty was founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, a former slave of Muhammad of Ghor, who became the first sultan of Delhi after Muhammad's death in 1206.
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lodi dynasty:-**

 
 
• It is also known as the Afghan dynasty, was a Pashtun dynasty that ruled over the Delhi Sultanate in India from 1451 to 1526.
 
• The dynasty was founded by Bahlul Khan Lodi, a Pashtun chief from Multan, who replaced the Sayyid dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Khalji dynasty:-**
 
 
• It was the second dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, ruling over large parts of the Indian subcontinent for nearly three decades between 1290 and 1320.
 
• It was founded by Jalal ud din Firuz Khalji, a Pashtun general from the region of Ghazni in present-day Afghanistan.
 
• The Khalji dynasty is noted for its military expansion, administrative reforms, and cultural patronage.
 
 
 
• **Tughlaq dynasty:-**
 
 
• It was the third dynasty to rule over the Delhi Sultanate in medieval India.
 
• It lasted from 1320 to 1413 and was known for its ambitious reforms and its eventual decline.

questions.question: Which of the following varieties of rice is known as the miracle rice for India and was first harvested in 1967 with exceptional yield?

__
 
• **IR8**:-

 
 
• **It is also known as "miracle rice," is a high-yielding semi-dwarf rice variety developed by the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) in the early 1960s. **
 
• It was developed by an IRRI team consisting of Jennings, Hank Beachell, Akira Tanaka, T.T. Chang, S.K. De Datta, and Robert Chandler.
 
• **The variety of rice known as the "miracle rice" for India is IR8.**
 
• It was capable of producing up to 5 tons of rice per hectare, a significant increase over the traditional tall rice varieties that yielded around 1-2 tons per hectare.
 
• This breakthrough in rice production marked the beginning of the Green Revolution in Asia, a period of agricultural advancements that transformed rice farming and alleviated food scarcity in the region.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) is an American animal rights organization based in Norfolk, Virginia, founded in 1980 by Ingrid Newkirk and Alex Pacheco. **
 
• PETA says that its entities have more than 9 million members globally.
 
• The organization claims to be "the largest animal rights organization in the world."
 
 
 
• **DGWG:-**
 
 
• **DGWG stands for Dee-geo-woo-gen, a recessive dwarfing gene in rice. **
 
• It is a single-gene mutation that causes a reduction in plant height by about 25%.
 
• DGWG has been used in rice breeding to create semi-dwarf varieties that are less prone to lodging, which is the bending or falling over of plants due to wind or heavy grain loads.

questions.question: On which of the following rivers does the National Waterway- 2 lie that covers the Sadiya - Dhubri stretch?

__
 
• **National Waterway-2:-**

 
 
• **NW-2 is a designated inland waterway in India that runs along the Brahmaputra River in the state of Assam.**
 
• It stretches for 891 kilometers (554 miles) from Dhubri on the Bangladesh border to Sadiya in the easternmost part of the state.
 
• NW-2 is one of the most important national waterways in India, providing a crucial transportation link for the northeastern region of the country. 
 
 
 
• **Brahmaputra River:-**
 
 
• The Brahmaputra, one of the largest rivers of the world, has its origin in the Chemayungdung glacier of the Kailash range near the Mansarovar lake.
 
• It emerges as a turbulent and dynamic river after carving out a deep gorge in the Central Himalayas near Namcha Barwa (7,755 m).
 
• The river emerges from the foothills under the name of Siang or Dihang. It enters India west of Sadiya town in Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• Flowing southwest, it receives its main left bank tributaries, viz., Dibang or Sikang and Lohit; thereafter, it is known as the Brahmaputra.
 
• The Brahmaputra River is a major source of water for irrigation and hydroelectric power, and it also supports a rich biodiversity of plants and animals.

• It originates in the Himalayas and flows through India and Bangladesh before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The Ganges River is a major source of water for irrigation and drinking water, and it also supports a rich biodiversity of plants and animals.

• The Krishna River is a major source of water for irrigation and hydroelectric power, and it also supports a rich agricultural economy.
 
 
 
• **Godavari River:-**
 
 
• It is the second longest river in India. It originates in the Western Ghats and flows through the states of Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Odisha before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The Godavari River is a major source of water for irrigation and drinking water, and it also supports a rich agricultural economy.

• **Pandit S. Ballesh Bhajantri:-**

 
 
• **He is an esteemed Indian classical Hindustani shehnai player.**
 
• He is regarded as a prominent figure in the Benares gharana style of shehnai playing and is also a Patiala gharana Hindustani vocalist, ghazal singer, Indian playback singer, and musician.

• The shehnai is known for its rich, vibrant sound, often described as "haunting" or "soulful."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghatam**:-

 
 
• **The ghatam is a percussion instrument originating from South India, traditionally associated with Carnatic classical music. **
 
• It is a clay pot that is struck with the hands or fingers to produce a variety of sounds, resembling the tabla, a two-headed drum.
 
• The ghatam is known for its rich, resonant timbre and its ability to produce a wide range of pitches.
 
• It is often used to accompany other instruments, such as the flute and the mridangam.

• It is a versatile instrument, used in both Carnatic and Hindustani classical music, as well as in folk and devotional music.
 
• The bansuri is known for its sweet, mellow sound and its ability to produce intricate melodies.
 
 
 
• **Mridangam**:-
 
 
• **The mridangam is a two-headed drum originating from South India, traditionally associated with Carnatic classical music. **
 
• It is considered the primary percussion instrument in Carnatic music, providing rhythmic accompaniment to the melody and improvisation.
 
• The mridangam is played with the hands and fingers, producing a wide range of sounds, from crisp slaps to deep resonant tones.
 
• It is known for its complex rhythmic patterns and its ability to follow and complement the intricacies of the melody.

questions.question: The Panjnad is the name given to the five rivers of Punjab, namely the Satluj, the Beas, the Ravi, the Chenab and the Jhelum. It finally discharges into which sea?

__
 
• **Arabian Sea:-**

 
 
• **The Arabian Sea, a vast body of water covering approximately 3,862,000 square kilometers (1,491,000 square miles).**
 
• It is a significant region of the northern Indian Ocean.
 
• **It is bounded by the Arabian Peninsula on the west, the Horn of Africa and the Gulf of Aden on the southwest, Iran and Pakistan on the north, India on the east, and the Laccadive Sea and the Maldives on the southeast.**
 
• The Arabian Sea plays a crucial role in the region's climate, economy, and biodiversity.
 
• **The Panjnad River, formed by the confluence of the five rivers of Punjab, ultimately discharges into the Arabian Sea.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Caspian Sea:-**

 
 
• The Caspian Sea is an endorheic lake, or a lake with no natural outlet to the ocean, located between Europe and Asia.
 
• It is the largest inland body of water in the world, with a surface area of 371,000 square kilometers (143,000 square miles).
 
• The Caspian Sea is bordered by Russia, Azerbaijan, Iran, Turkmenistan, and Kazakhstan.
 
 
 
• **Andaman Sea:-**
 
 
• The Andaman Sea is a marginal sea of the northeastern Indian Ocean, bounded by the coastlines of Myanmar and Thailand along the Gulf of Martaban and the western side of the Malay Peninsula, and separated from the Bay of Bengal by the Great Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• It has an area of 797,000 square kilometers (308,000 square miles), with an average depth of 4,700 meters (15,400 feet).
 
 
 
• **Red Sea:-**
 
 
• The Red Sea is a narrow elongated basin of the Indian Ocean, extending northeastward from the Gulf of Aden at the southern tip of the Arabian Peninsula to the Suez Canal at the head of the Gulf of Suez.
 
• It has an area of 458,000 square kilometers (177,000 square miles), with an average depth of 200 meters (660 feet) and a maximum depth of 2,520 meters (8,268 feet).

questions.question: Which of the following tests is used to confirm the presence of typhoid fever?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Widal Test**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Widal Test:-**

 
 
• **The Widal test is a blood test used to diagnose typhoid fever. **
 
• **It was developed by Carl Widal in 1896.**
 
• In the Widal test, the patient's blood is tested for antibodies that are produced against Salmonella typhi, the bacteria that causes typhoid fever. If antibodies are found in the patient's blood, this may be a sign of typhoid fever.
 
• The Widal test can be used to diagnose typhoid fever, but it is not always accurate. A negative result does not mean that the patient does not have typhoid fever. In addition, a positive result does not mean that the patient currently has typhoid fever. A positive result may also indicate that the patient has recently recovered from typhoid fever.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **C-reactive protein (CRP):-**

 
 
• The C-reactive protein (CRP) test is a blood test that measures the level of C-reactive protein in your blood.
 
• CRP is a protein produced by your liver. The level of CRP in your blood increases when there is inflammation in your body. Inflammation is a natural response to injury or infection.
 
• It helps your body heal and protect itself from further damage. However, chronic inflammation can be harmful and lead to health problems such as heart disease, stroke, and cancer.
 
 
 
• **Vivax test:-**
 
 
• The Vivax test is a rapid diagnostic test (RDT) used to detect Plasmodium vivax, the most common species of malaria outside of Africa.
 
• The test works by detecting antigens, which are proteins produced by the malaria parasite, in the patient's blood.

questions.question: Who among the following is known as the ‘Father of the Green Revolution’ in the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Norman Borlaug.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Norman Borlaug:-

 
 
• The "Father of the Green Revolution" is typically attributed to an American agronomist named Norman Borlaug.
 
• Borlaug was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 in recognition of his contributions to world peace through increasing food supply.
 
• His pioneering work introducing high-yielding and disease-resistant wheat varieties combined with modern agricultural production techniques to Mexico, Pakistan, and India led these countries to greatly increase their food production and to serve as examples for the global Green Revolution.
 
• His work is estimated to have saved a billion people from starvation worldwide.
 
 
 
• Green Revolution:-
 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to a series of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives, occurring between the 1950s and the late 1960s, that increased agricultural production worldwide, particularly in the developing world.
 
• The term "Green Revolution" was first used in 1968 by former United States Agency for International Development (USAID) director William Gaud, who noted the spread of the new technologies and said, "These and other developments in the field of agriculture contain the makings of a new revolution.
 
• It is not a violent Red Revolution like that of the Soviets, nor is it a White Revolution like that of the Shah of Iran. I call it the Green Revolution."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Ralph Bunche:-

 
 
• He was an American political scientist, diplomat, and leading U.S. civil rights activist.
 
• He received the 1950 Nobel Peace Prize for his late 1940s mediation in Palestine.
 
• He was the first African American and person of color to be so honored in the history of the prize.
 
 
 
• Linus Carl Pauling:-
 
 
• He was an American chemist, biochemist, peace activist, author, and educator.
 
• He was one of the most influential chemists in history and is considered one of the greatest scientists of the 20th century.
 
• His work contributed significantly to the understanding of the nature of the chemical bond and the structure of molecules and crystals.
 
 
 
• Dr. M.S. Swaminathan:-
 
 
• He is an Indian geneticist and international administrator, renowned for his leading role in India's "Green Revolution," a program under which high-yield varieties of wheat and rice seedlings were planted in the fields of poor farmers.

questions.question: What is the maximum age for a member of a joint public service commission to hold his / her office as per the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**62 Years.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ** Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC):**

 
 
• The Constitution makes a provision for the establishment of a Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC) for two or more states.
 
• While the UPSC and the SPSC are created directly by the Constitution, a JSPSC can be created by an act of Parliament at the request of the state legislatures concerned. 
 
• Thus, a JSPSC is a statutory and not a constitutional body.
 
• The two states of Punjab and Haryana had a JSPSC for a short period, after the creation of Haryana out of Punjab in 1966.
 
• The chairman and members of a JSPSC are appointed by the president.
 
• They hold office for a term of six years or until they attain the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier.
 
• They can be suspended or removed by the president.
 
• They can also resign from their offices at any time by submitting their resignation letters to the president.
 
• The number of members of a JSPSC and their conditions of service is determined by the president.
 
• A JSPSC presents its annual performance report to each of the concerned state governors.
 
• Each governor places the report before the state legislature.
 
• The UPSC can also serve the needs of a state at the request of the state governor and with the approval of the president.
 
• As provided by the Government of India Act of 1919, a Central Public Service Commission was set up in 1926 and entrusted with the task of recruiting civil servants.
 
• The Government of India Act of 1935 provided for the establishment of not only a Federal Public Service Commission but also a Provincial Public Service Commission and Joint Public Service Commission for two or more provinces.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about the circular flow of income in a two - sector economy?

options.text: Total production is equal to total consumption.
Factor payment is equal to factor income.
Real Flow is more than money flow.
Consumption expenditure is equal to factor income.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Real Flow is more than money flow.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In a two-sector economy:-**

 
 
• **Real flow refers to the physical movement of goods and services between households and firms, while money flow refers to the monetary payments made for these goods and services. **
 
• In a closed economy without savings or investment, real flow and money flow are always equal.
 
• This is because the total value of goods and services produced (real flow) must be equal to the total amount of money spent on those goods and services (money flow).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Total production is equal to total consumption:-**

 
 
• This is because, in a closed economy without savings or investment, all goods and services produced are eventually consumed.
 
 
 
• **Factor payment is equal to factor income:-**
 
 
• This is because factor payments are the payments made to households for their factors of production (land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship), and factor income is the income that households receive from these factors.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Consumption expenditure is equal to factor income:-** This is because in a closed economy without savings or investment, all income is eventually spent on consumption.

questions.question: Which ecological law states that body form or shape is linear in warm climates and more rounded and compact in cold climates?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Allen's Rule.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Allen's rule:-**

 
 
• **It is an ecogeographical rule that states that endothermic animals living in colder climates tend to have shorter appendages (limbs, tails, ears, etc.) and a more compact body shape than those living in warmer climates. **
 
• This is because a smaller surface area to volume ratio minimizes heat loss in cold environments.
 
• For example, polar bears have shorter ears and legs than brown bears, which live in warmer climates. This allows them to conserve body heat more effectively in the Arctic.
 
• Allen's rule is one of several adaptations that help animals survive in cold climates. Other adaptations include thicker fur, a higher metabolic rate, and the ability to store fat.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yoda's rule:-**

 
 
• It (also known as the self-thinning rule or the 3/2 power law) states that in a population of sessile organisms (organisms that cannot move), the relationship between the average individual size and the population density is a negative power law with a slope of -3/2. 
 
 
 
• **Jordan's rule:-**
 
 
• It states that the number of vertebrae in fishes increases with latitude. This means that fish found in colder waters tend to have more vertebrae than fish found in warmer waters. This is thought to be an adaptation to help fish conserve body heat in colder temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Gloger's rule:-**
 
 
• It states that in ectotherms (cold-blooded animals), the amount of melanin in the skin is inversely proportional to the temperature of the environment.
 
• This means that animals that live in colder environments tend to have darker skin than animals that live in warmer environments. This is thought to be an adaptation to help animals absorb more heat from the sun in colder temperatures.

questions.question: Which of the following is a function performed by commercial banks in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Credit creation.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Credit creation:-**

 
 
• **It is the process of lending money to create new money in the economy. **
 
• **Commercial banks do this by accepting deposits from customers and then lending out a portion of those deposits to other customers.**
 
• When a bank lends money, it creates a new loan asset on its balance sheet and a new deposit liability.
 
• This new deposit can then be used by the borrower to spend money, which in turn creates new deposits for other banks. In this way, commercial banks play a key role in the money supply.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Issue of currency:-**

 
 
• It is a function of the central bank, not commercial banks.
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is responsible for issuing currency in India.**
 
 
 
• **Banking facilities to the government:-**
 
 
• It is a function of both commercial banks and the central bank.
 
• **Commercial banks provide banking services to the government, such as collecting taxes and making payments. **
 
• The RBI also provides banking services to the government, such as managing the government's debt.
 
 
 
• **Credit control:-**
 
 
• It is a function of the central bank.
 
• **The RBI uses credit control measures to manage the money supply and inflation.**

questions.question: Salt Satyagraha was associated with the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Disobedience Movement.__** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Salt Satyagraha:-**

 
 
• **It is also known as the Salt March or Dandi March, was a significant act of nonviolent civil disobedience led by Mahatma Gandhi in colonial India. **
 
• The 24-day march, which lasted from March 12 to April 5, 1930, was a direct action campaign of tax resistance and nonviolent protest against the British salt monopoly. 
 
• **Gandhi and his followers walked over 240 miles from Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad to Dandi, a coastal village in Gujarat, to make salt from seawater.**
 
• This act of defiance was a symbolic protest against the British Salt Acts of 1882, which gave the British government a monopoly on the production and sale of salt in India.
 
• The Salt Satyagraha had a profound impact on the Indian independence movement.
 
• It galvanized public support for Gandhi and his philosophy of nonviolence, and it brought international attention to the struggle for Indian independence.
 
• The march also inspired other nonviolent resistance movements around the world.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quit India Movement:-**

 
 
• The Quit India Movement was a nonviolent civil disobedience movement launched in August 1942 to demand the immediate withdrawal of British rule from India.
 
• The movement was led by Mahatma Gandhi and the Indian National Congress.
 
 
 
• **Champaran Satyagraha:-**
 
 
• The Champaran Satyagraha was a farmer's uprising that took place in Champaran district of Bihar, India, in 1917.
 
• The farmers were protesting against the British indigo planters' exploitative system of forced cultivation and low prices.
 
 
 
• **Kheda Satyagraha:-**
 
 
• The Kheda Satyagraha was a nonviolent peasant movement that took place in Kheda, Gujarat, India, in 1918.
 
• The peasants were protesting against the British government's insistence on collecting taxes despite the widespread damage caused by a famine.

questions.question: Which is the largest river of peninsular India?

__
 
• **Godavari**:-

 
 
• **The largest river of peninsular India is the Godavari River. **
 
• **It is also known as the "Dakshin Ganga" (Southern Ganges) and is the second-longest river in India after the Ganges. **
 
• The Godavari River has a total length of 1,465 kilometers (914 miles) and drains a basin of about 1,10,000 square kilometers (42,400 square miles).
 
• **The Godavari River originates in the Western Ghats near Nashik, Maharashtra, and flows eastward across peninsular India. **
 
• It passes through the states of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Odisha before finally draining into the Bay of Bengal near Rajahmundry, Andhra Pradesh. The Godavari River is a major source of irrigation and hydroelectricity in peninsular India.
 
• It is also considered sacred by Hindus and is home to numerous temples and pilgrimage sites.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **The Tapi River, formerly known as the Tapti River, is the ninth-longest river in India. **
 
• It flows from the Satpura Hills in Maharashtra and drains into the Gulf of Cambay in Gujarat.
 
• The river is 724 kilometers (450 miles) long and drains a basin of 109,000 square kilometers (42,000 square miles).
 
 
 
• **Tungabhadra River:-**
 
 
• **The Tungabhadra River is a major tributary of the Krishna River in India. **
 
• It is formed by the confluence of the Bhadra and Tunga rivers in the Western Ghats.
 
• The Tungabhadra River flows eastward for 524 kilometers (326 miles) before joining the Krishna River near Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Krishna River:-**
 
 
• **The Krishna River is the Third-longest river in India and the second-longest river in peninsular India after the Godavari River. **
 
• It originates in the Western Ghats near Mahabaleshwar, Maharashtra, and flows eastward for 1,400 kilometers (870 miles) before draining into the Bay of Bengal near Machilipatnam, Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The Krishna River drains a basin of 216,000 square kilometers (83,000 square miles).
